text:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a bunch of mem profiling on long-running continuous batches (seq mean ~1024, spikes to 4096). seeing unexpectedly high reserved memory as batch grows. attaching summary below.

jon: can you paste the perf counters?

maya: paste of top lines from `cuda_mem_report` (trimmed):
```
model: llama-13b
batch_size: 64 -> 96 growth window
reserved_bytes: 13.2 GB
active_bytes: 8.5 GB
padding_waste: 2.7 GB (20% of tokens)
per_seq_overhead: 45 KB
kv_cache_reserved: 1.6 GB (not all used)
fragmentation_est: ~0.9 GB
```

maya: main suspicion: allocator is rounding up workspaces and also reserving for worst-case KV cache per sample instead of actual live kv usage. so reserved_bytes >> active_bytes when batch grows.

sahil: yep that matches what I saw on the repro traces. continuous batching adds sequences incrementally, we pad to the longest in batch which multiplies padding_waste quickly. the allocator then expands workspace pools to accommodate peak seq len and doesn't shrink between requests because of soft retention.

olivia: curious — how much of the reserved is from workspace vs from per-request temp buffers? can we split accounting?

maya: I added a quick metric in the runtime: `mem.{model}.{kind}` where kind = reserved|active|workspace|kv_reserved|kv_active|fragments. for one run (64->96):
```
mem.llama13b.reserved=13.2GB
mem.llama13b.active=8.5GB
mem.llama13b.workspace=4.1GB
mem.llama13b.kv_reserved=1.6GB
mem.llama13b.kv_active=0.7GB
mem.llama13b.fragmentation=0.3GB
```

jon: interesting, workspace is big chunk. looks like allocator is sizing workspace per-batch to (max_seq * batch) with padding accounting double-counting maybe.

maya: exact. two things we discovered: (1) per-sequence prefix metadata (KV pointers, small structs) is counted into `per_seq_overhead` and multiplied by batch (2) workspace allocator uses per-device bins; when multiple streams overlap, reserved grows past sum of active.

ryan: proposals:
- track `reserved_by_policy` vs `reserved_by_allocator`. attribute reservations that are held for policy reasons (min_workspace for model config, soft retention) vs allocations from current batch.
- add sliding shrinker: if `active_bytes < reserved_bytes * 0.6` for N seconds, try releasing largest workspace back to OS or split the largest bin.
- change padding strategy: use per-request heuristics to limit pad to p-th percentile of recent seq lengths instead of max when tail is spiky.

olivia: p-th percentile pad sounds good for latency-sensitive callers? might regress 99p latency if we truncate too aggressively. can we make it per-route config?

maya: yes route-level policy. default: `pad_policy: conservative` (max), `pad_policy: auto_95` (95th percentile), `pad_policy: latency_99_guarded` with occasional fallback to a larger workspace.

jon: also KV cache: we reserved kv slots for worst-case sequence length per sample. if we keep per-sample kv usage counters we could avoid reserving the full kv capacity until we actually see attention steps that need it. ie lazy kv reservation.

maya: implemented a prototype: lazy-kv which reserves small header for each sample and grows kv allocations on-demand. result: kv_reserved dropped 60% in our run but increased a tiny bit of alloc churn.

sahil: how did that affect throughput/latency?

maya: throughput unchanged in steady-state, tail 99p latency increased ~3-5% when lazy-alloc had to grow KV mid-request on rare long sequences. but overall mem headroom improved so we could fit bigger batches.

olivia: tradeoff seems acceptable with route-level opt-in. can we document metrics to observe regressions?

maya: added these metrics: `mem.pad_waste_ratio`, `mem.kv_lazy_grow_count`, `allocator.shrink_ops`, `allocator.bin_fill_ratio`. Also a histogram `batch.effective_seq_len` to compute percentile for auto pad policy.

ryan: good. second issue: fragmentation. allocator bins cause fragmentation when we free large buffers but keep smaller ones. any idea for reuse policy?

maya: simple improvement: try coalescing small free blocks into larger ones before returning to OS. also add a fast-path for reusing last-freed workspace if size within +/-10% of requested. that reduced fragmentation estimate by ~300MB in tests.

jon: we should also account for per-seq small objects separately in telemetry (they're small but N is large) — add `mem.per_seq_structs` and surface per-route cost computed as `per_seq_structs * avg_batch`.

maya: agreed. I'll open a PR with metrics, default pad_policy auto_95, lazy-kv gated behind a feature flag per-route, and shrinker with conservative thresholds (60% after 30s).

olivia: can you include a small config example in the PR?

maya: sure, snippet I'll add: 
```
route: "/chat"
model: llama-13b
mem:
  pad_policy: auto_95
  kv_policy: lazy
  shrinker:
    enabled: true
    threshold_ratio: 0.6
    idle_secs: 30
```

sahil: tests to add: OOM regression matrix (varied seq distributions, spike patterns), and stress test ensuring lazy-kv growth doesn't cause frequent reallocs.

maya: adding perf runs to CI job `runtime_mem_stress` and a flakiness guard. will also add dashboards for the new metrics and alerts when `mem.pad_waste_ratio > 0.25` or `allocator.bin_fill_ratio < 0.2` for 2 mins.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for branch mem/telemetry-pad-95 on docker-tag runtime-mem-2026-03-17-canary

jon: awesome. one more ask — can we include a small visualization of batch growth over time in the dashboard? x=time, lines: reserved vs active vs workspace. it's the easiest way for SRE to spot leaks.

maya: yup adding timeseries and percentiles. I'll follow up with the PR link once ready. :thumbsup:
